newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala peace talks to begin Friday in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala peace talks to begin Friday in Mexico.

text.p: Government peace negotiators said on Thursday they will meet leftist rebels in Mexico on Friday to continue peace negotiations aimed at reaching a definitive peace agreement later this year.

Top government negotiator Gustavo Porras told reporters the talks will focus, for the fourth time since June, on the themes of strengthening the civilian government and the role of the army in peacetime.
"We have reached a fundamental consensus, especially on the theme of strengthening civilian power," said Porras.
The government and the Guatemalan Revolutionary Unit (URNG) have held sporadic peace talks since 1991 to end 36 years of civil war in which 100,000 people have died and more than 40,000 disappeared.
Talks intensified this year and the two sides have signed six of 11 planned accords within a larger agreement.
Porras said negotiators will sign agreements on the role of the army and strengthening civilian government in Mexico by Sept. 15, when both countries celebrate independence day.
Later in the year the negotiators plan to sign in Madrid an accord regarding the return of URNG combatants to legal, political life. A ceasefire accord will be signed in Oslo, said Porras.
